production.note: US model years 1993-1995. Previously recorded as calendar years 1991-2002: Global production of the FD. Start: Mazda states the third-generation RX-7 was launched in 1991. End year 2002 is from Evo ('produced between 1992 and 2002') and Grassroots Motorsports (sold in Japan through the 2002 model year); the Mazda page opened does not give an end year. Sold in the US for model years 1993-1995 only.

body.note: Consumer Guide lists it as a 2-door hatchback (it has a glass rear hatch); recorded as Coupe.

transmission.note: US market: 5-speed manual standard, 4-speed automatic optional

powerHp.note: Mazda USA states 255 hp; Grassroots Motorsports and Consumer Guide list the same 255 hp (at 6,500 rpm) for the 1993-1995 US car. Later Japan-market cars were rated higher.

weightLb.note: Base model with 5-speed manual, the lightest standard US configuration, from the publication's spec panel. Edmunds lists the same 2,789 lb for the 1993 base car.

sources.title: Mazda RX-7 Heaven: Legendary Rotary Sports Car
Buyer's guide: third-generation FD-chassis Mazda RX-7

discrepancies.reason: Mazda USA's retrospective article says 'at just 2,850 lbs' without naming a trim, transmission or model year; 2,789 lb is given specifically for the US base model with the 5-speed manual.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 2,789 lb: it names the configuration (lightest standard US car) and two independent sources agree.

discrepancies.reason: Mazda dates the launch of the third generation to 1991 (Japan); Evo counts from 1992, when export sales began (Grassroots Motorsports: launched in 1992 as an early 1993 model in the US).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the manufacturer's 1991 start and the 2002 end that Evo and Grassroots Motorsports agree on.
